sections.h2: Where is Niles and how did the village take shape?
sections.html:
Niles is a village in Cook County that sits against the far northwest edge of Chicago. It lies in Maine and Niles townships, covers 5.85 square miles, and has Skokie to the east, Morton Grove to the northeast, Glenview to the north and Park Ridge to the west. Milwaukee Avenue runs diagonally through the middle, and the North Branch of the Chicago River crosses the eastern part.

Settlers arrived in 1827, and the place was first called Dutchman's Point for the German immigrants who followed. The village was incorporated on August 24, 1899 with about 500 residents. Postwar housing did the rest: the census counted 3,587 people in 1950 and 20,393 in 1960, and the 1970 count of 31,432 remains the peak. The 2020 count was 30,912, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 30,443.

Former farms and nurseries were redeveloped into housing during that burst, so much of what sellers here own dates from the postwar years.

sections.h2: What taxes are due at a Niles closing?
sections.html:
Three transfer tax layers can apply to a Niles sale. The village's page prints its rate as $3.00 per $1,000 of price, and says the buyer pays it. The state and county rates come from the Cook County Clerk's transfer fee page.

LayerRate as printedParty liable
State of Illinois.50 per $500Seller
Cook County.25 per $500Seller
Village of Niles$3.00 per $1,000, or fraction thereofBuyer

An exempt stamp, for a deed that is not a sale, costs a flat $25.00 and cannot be issued until all outstanding fines and fees are paid. To get either stamp, the village requires a completed Niles Real Estate Transfer Declaration Form and a copy of the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.

sections.h2: What does a Niles seller have to do before the transfer stamp is issued?
sections.html:
Call the Finance Department at 847-588-8030 ten days before closing. The village uses that call to arrange a final water reading and a property search for fines, fees or violations.

The village will not issue a stamp unless the property is free of liens and violations and has no outstanding bills owed to the village. Its page lists these practical points:

  • Stamps can be bought in person at the Finance Department in Niles Village Hall, or by mail to 1000 Civic Center Drive with a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope.
  • In-person transactions must reach the Finance Department before 4:30 pm with paperwork already complete.
  • Accepted payment includes a cashier's check, money order, title company check, attorney firm check, cash, or a credit or debit card with a processing fee.
  • Completed forms can be emailed to the village's real estate transfer stamp address, with the property address in the subject line. Water reading and property search requests must be phoned in, not emailed.

A lien, an unpaid water bill or an open code violation will stop the stamp, so ask the Finance Department for the property search result early enough to fix anything that turns up.

sections.h2: What happens to a Niles rental when it is sold?
sections.html:
If the transfer declarations show the new owner will not live there, the buyer must file a Rental License Application when buying the transfer stamp. The village's page also says rental licenses are non-transferable when a property is sold, so the license you hold does not pass to the buyer.

That affects a landlord selling to another investor and a family selling a house that will be rented out. Questions about the application go to Community Development at 847-588-8040. A seller who has a tenant in place should also check the lease and ask the buyer's side how it plans to apply for the license, since the application is filed when the stamp is bought.

sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax rebate for Niles residents who buy again in the village?
sections.html:
Yes, for a narrow group. The village's rebate form describes a rebate of $2 per $1,000 for a Niles resident who sold a principal residence and buys a residential structure in the village to use as a principal residence. The form says the rebate equals two-thirds of the amount paid for the transfer stamp on the new property.

The buyer files it after closing, with proof of the transaction, within one year of the sale of the old residence. The Finance Director reviews the claim, and commercial and retail property do not qualify. A homeowner who is selling in Niles to move up or down within the village should keep the closing statements from both deals.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Niles homes and households?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 and 2025 figures include:

  • Owner-occupied rate: 74.6%.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $358,700.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $2,159 with a mortgage and $844 without.
  • Median gross rent: $1,336.
  • Households: 11,481, with 2.51 persons per household.
  • Median household income: $75,274, and 28.5% of residents are 65 or older.
  • Foreign-born residents: 42.0%, and 59.5% of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home.

The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 1.6% below the April 2020 base.

sections.h2: What else do buyers weigh when they look at a Niles house?
sections.html:
Services and location carry a lot of weight in a village this compact. Niles started the first free ambulance service in Illinois in 1946, and it later added the free bus. It was named an All-America City in 1964.

The Tam O'Shanter Golf Course, owned by the Niles Park District, hosted the All American Open on the PGA Tour from 1941 to 1957 and the Western Open in 1964 and 1965. St. Adalbert Cemetery is the largest in the Archdiocese of Chicago by burials. Niles has four sister cities: Pisa in Italy, Nafplion in Greece, Leixlip in Ireland and Limanowa in Poland.

Retail is a strength as well. The Census Bureau lists 2022 retail sales of about $2.1 billion, or $70,862 per resident, a high per-capita figure for a village of this size.

sections.h2: Which schools, buses and employers define Niles?
sections.html:
Several elementary districts cover the village: East Maine District 63, Park Ridge-Niles District 64, Golf District 67, Niles District 71 and Fairview District 72. High school students attend Maine Township District 207 or Niles Township Community District 219, and Oakton Community College is the local community college district. Notre Dame College Prep and Northridge Preparatory School are Catholic high schools in the village's education listing.

Niles runs a free village bus, and Pace operates its Pulse Milwaukee and Pulse Dempster lines through town. U.S. 14 and Illinois routes 21, 43 and 58 cross the village. The Leaning Tower of Niles, a scaled replica of the tower in Pisa, is its best-known landmark, and Golf Mill Shopping Center opened in 1960.

The village's 2019 financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, listed Woodward with 1,000 employees, Shure with 680, Bradford Exchange with 600 and Coca-Cola Bottling with 500 as leading employers.

faqs.q: Who pays the Niles real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer pays the village stamp, at $3.00 per $1,000 of price or fraction thereof. The Cook County Clerk's table lists the state ($.50 per $500) and the county ($.25 per $500) as the seller's responsibility.

faqs.q: How early should I call the village before closing on a Niles house?
faqs.a: Ten days before closing. The Finance Department asks the seller to call 847-588-8030 so it can take a final water reading and run a property search for fines, fees and violations.

faqs.q: Can a Niles stamp be issued with an unpaid water bill or violation on the property?
faqs.a: No. The village says the property must be free of liens and violations and cannot have outstanding bills owed to the village. Exempt stamps are also held until all fines and fees are paid.

faqs.q: What does a Niles buyer need if the house will be a rental?
faqs.a: A Rental License Application, filed at the time the transfer stamp is bought. Rental licenses do not carry over to the buyer when a property is sold.

faqs.q: Does Niles refund any of the transfer tax?
faqs.a: Only to a Niles resident who sold a principal residence and buys another residence in the village, and only on the form filed within one year. The rebate is $2 per $1,000, calculated as two-thirds of the stamp price paid on the new property.
